questions.prompt: When should a story be shortened?
questions.answer: When the listener's purpose or time favours concise information.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Constructs an accurate, coherent, bounded narrative without presenting anecdotes as general proof or exposing private information.
scoring.transfer: Prepare a fictional 60-second story and a written 100-word equivalent. Use a clear sequence, distinguish observation from interpretation, protect privacy and state one limitation. Explain when direct evidence should replace the anecdote.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
